output.summary: KEP-589 introduces a built-in Lease API (coordination.k8s.io) so each Kubelet's node heartbeat is a small Lease object updated independently of NodeStatus, with NodeController treating both as health signals. The KEP's status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Large clusters (more than 2000 nodes) hit etcd database size limits because node heartbeats were large Node objects stored in full on every 10s update. Making heartbeats a small Lease object reduces etcd size while preserving NotReady and eviction behavior. The design chose a built-in API over a CRD because CRDs lacked versioning and were slower, lacking protobuf support.

alternatives.option: Use kube-system namespace for the heartbeat objects
alternatives.why_not: The design says kube-system is already too overloaded, so a dedicated namespace was created instead.

alternatives.option: Use a CRD instead of a built-in API
alternatives.why_not: The readme says CRDs do not yet have versioning support, are significantly less performant (no protobuf support), and it was unknown whether storage could later move from a CRD to a built-in API.

evidence.quote: Kubelet creates and periodically updates its own Lease object and frequency of those updates is independent from NodeStatus update frequency.
even though CRDs are `the new way` for creating new APIs, they don't yet have versioning support and are significantly less performant
Implementation is finished. Documentation is merged into https://github.com/kubernetes/website/blob/dev-1.13/content/en/docs/concepts/architecture/nodes.md
the current focus is use of the API for node presence detection (aka "heartbeats"), which is orthogonal to the pre-existing uses of LeaderElectionRecord
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2598 is the PR that moved this KEP to implemented.
